items.text: Under MCL 500.2006(3), how long does an insurer have to specify in writing what it needs for a satisfactory proof of loss?
30 days after receipt of a claim, unless the claim is settled within those 30 days.
What triggers the 30-day clock in MCL 500.2006(3), the notice of loss or the proof of loss?
The notice of loss. The clock runs from receipt of a claim, not from receipt of a proof of loss.
A homeowner reports a water loss on January 6 but the insurer never sends anything in writing about what it needs for a satisfactory proof of loss. What happens after February 5?

February 5 is 30 days after notice, so the insurer has breached its written-specification duty under MCL 500.2006(3). The statute attaches no automatic consequence, and Griswold does not say silence makes a later proof of loss satisfactory; it says satisfactory proof of loss is a question of fact. What you get is a dated statutory breach, no carrier document list to be held to later, and evidence of the delay practices DIFS names in Bulletin 2025-25-INS.
If a proof of loss covers only part of a claim, when is that partial amount considered timely paid under MCL 500.2006(3)?
If paid within 60 days after the insurer's receipt of that partial proof of loss. Any remainder submitted later gets its own 60-day clock from its own receipt date.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(j), what must a mortgagee do if the insured fails to render a proof of loss?
Upon notice from the insurer, the mortgagee must render its own proof of loss within 60 days after the notice.
A homeowner submits her own sworn proof of loss on February 1. Does the mortgagee's 60-day proof-of-loss clock under MCL 500.2833(1)(j) ever start?
No. That clock only triggers when the insured fails to render a proof of loss and the insurer then notifies the mortgagee. Because the homeowner supplied her own, it never fires.
What does MCL 500.2833(1)(l) require a fire policy to contain about notice of loss, and does it set a day count?
It requires the policy to contain the notification requirements when a loss occurs. It sets no day count; the policy's own Conditions section sets the insured's reporting deadline.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(p), how many days after receipt of proof of amount of loss must a fire insurance loss be paid?
30 days, except as otherwise provided in section 2845.
MCL 500.2836(2) restates the 30-day payment rule. Quote it.

'Except as otherwise provided in section 2845, losses under any fire insurance policy shall be paid within 30 days after receipt of proof of the amount of the loss, notwithstanding the provisions of any contract or statute to the contrary.'
Under MCL 500.2006(4), when does 12% simple interest start accruing on unpaid benefits owed to a first-party insured?
From a date 60 days after satisfactory proof of loss was received by the insurer.
TRAP: A claim is paid on day 45 after proof of amount of loss. Is the insurer both late on the payment clock and liable for 12% interest?

No. Payment on day 45 is late under the 30-day payment clock, which runs from receipt of proof of the amount of loss (MCL 500.2833(1)(p), MCL 500.2836(2)). Interest under MCL 500.2006(4) runs only from a date 60 days after satisfactory proof of loss was received, so a claim paid on day 45 owes no interest. Watch the two triggers: proof of the amount of loss versus satisfactory proof of loss. They are usually the same document but they are not the same words.
Does the 'reasonably in dispute' defense in MCL 500.2006(4) apply to a first-party insured's claim for 12% interest?

No. That defense is written only into the third-party tort claimant sentence of subsection (4). First-party insureds get the 12% interest even if the claim is genuinely disputed, per Griswold Properties LLC v Lexington Ins Co, 276 Mich App 551 (2007), and Nickola v MIC General Ins Co, 500 Mich 115 (2017).
TRAP: Does a restoration contractor holding an assignment of benefits automatically get the 12% interest under MCL 500.2006(4)?

No. No published Michigan case found extends 'a person directly entitled to benefits' to a contractor-assignee on a property claim. The 12% is the insured's right, pursued derivatively at best by an assignee. Young v Michigan Mutual Ins Co, 139 Mich App 600 (1984), confirms the insured herself can sue to recover the section 2006 interest penalty.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), how many days does a party have to name a competent, independent appraiser after receiving a written appraisal demand?
20 days.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), if the two appraisers cannot agree on an umpire within how many days, may either side ask a circuit judge to select one?
15 days.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), which circuit court has authority to appoint an umpire if the appraisers cannot agree?
A judge of the circuit court for the county in which the loss occurred or in which the property is located.
How many of the three appraisal participants (two appraisers and an umpire) must sign a written agreement to set the amount of loss?
Any 2 of the 3.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), who pays each appraiser, and how is the umpire's cost split?
Each party pays its own appraiser. Other expenses of the appraisal and the umpire's compensation are split equally between the insured and the insurer.
TRAP: Does an appraisal award under MCL 500.2833(1)(m) decide whether a loss is covered?

No. Appraisal decides amount only, never coverage. Auto-Owners Ins Co v Kwaiser, 190 Mich App 482 (1991): 'We conclude that the issue of coverage is for the court, not the appraisers. The appraisal process cannot legally settle coverage issues.'
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(i), how many days' mailed notice must an insurer give before canceling a fire policy?
Not less than 10 days, mailed to the insured's last known address with postage fully prepaid.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(i), what is the minimum earned premium on an insurer-initiated cancellation?
The pro rata premium for the expired time, or $25.00, whichever is greater.
TRAP: Is MCL 500.2833(1)(i)'s 10-day cancellation notice the only rule that governs cancelling a Michigan homeowners policy?

No. That 10 days is the fire policy's mandatory contract term, what the policy must say. The Essential Insurance Act's MCL 500.2123 is an effectiveness rule: a termination is not effective without at least 30 days' notice, or 20 days if the notice goes out inside the policy's first 55 days. 'Termination' is defined at MCL 500.2104(5) as a refusal to continue to insure for reasons other than nonpayment. For a non-nonpayment home-insurance cancellation the 30 days is the longer number and so the operative one, which is how DIFS reads it in Bulletin 2025-12-INS. Whether 2833(1)(i)'s 10 days ever independently controls once 2123 applies is not resolved by any Michigan case found: INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
Under MCL 500.2103(3), what does 'home insurance' mean, and what does it exclude?

Fire insurance for an eligible dwelling type, plus endorsed non-business coverages, plus other residence coverages the director designates by rule. It excludes insurance for commercial, industrial, professional, or business property, obligations, or liabilities.
Under MCL 500.2103(2), who is an 'eligible person' for home insurance?

The owner-occupant or tenant of a house, condominium unit, cooperative unit, room, or apartment, or the owner-occupant of a multiple-unit dwelling of not more than 4 residential units, subject to listed disqualifiers such as a recent arson conviction or a fraud-based denied claim.
Under MCL 500.2117, an insurer's home-insurance underwriting rules for refusal, limitation, or nonrenewal must be based only on what kind of list?

A closed list in the statute: eligibility criteria, code-tied physical-condition standards, a 3-year claim history tied to negligence or an uncorrected hazard, market-value/replacement-cost ratios, a claim-history threshold for nonrenewal, mismatched unit counts, extended vacancy with intent to vacate, a changed adjacent hazard, underinsurance below an 80% condition of sale, or a reported threat or assault against insurer personnel.
Under MCL 500.2117's nonrenewal claim-history threshold, how many paid claims in the preceding 3 years, and totaling how much, may support a nonrenewal of home insurance?

3 paid claims within the preceding 3 years totaling at least $5,000 excluding weather-related claims, or at least $6,600 including them. Careful: MCL 500.2117(2)(e)(i) still prints $3,000 and $4,000, but subsection (5) indexes those to the consumer price index every sixth year by DIFS bulletin, and DIFS Bulletin 2024-02-INS certified $5,000 and $6,600 effective January 1, 2024. Next adjustment due January 1, 2030.
TRAP: Under DIFS Bulletin 2025-12-INS, can a carrier cancel or nonrenew a home insurance policy because aerial imagery shows roof discoloration or streaking?
No. The bulletin states that mere cosmetic roof issues, such as discoloration or streaking, are not valid grounds for policy cancellation or nonrenewal.
Under MCL 500.2119, how must an insurer's underwriting rules be maintained and applied?
In writing, filed with the commissioner, and applied uniformly and without exception throughout the state.
Under MCL 500.2122, what must an insurer or agent do when declining to insure an applicant?

Inform the applicant of each specific reason for the declination, in writing if the application was written, or orally with a written explanation on request within 90 days if the application was oral.
Under MCL 500.2123(1), how many days' advance written notice must an insurer give before a termination of insurance is effective?

At least 30 days prior to the date of termination, delivered or mailed to the named insured at the person's last known address, stating the effective date and each specific reason for the termination. MCL 500.2123(4) adds a second gate: the termination is not effective unless its reasons conform to the insurer's own underwriting rules for that insurance.
Under MCL 500.2123(2), what shorter notice period applies to a policy in its first 55 days?
A notice of termination mailed or delivered within the first 55 days after initial issuance may be made effective not less than 20 days after the date of mailing or delivery.
Under MCL 500.2123(3), what day count governs a notice of termination for nonpayment of premium?
None fixed in the statute. It is effective as provided in the policy.
How does DIFS Bulletin 2025-12-INS connect MCL 500.2123 and MCL 500.2117 for home insurance cancellation?

The bulletin states that if an insurer intends to cancel or nonrenew a non-group policy for reasons other than nonpayment of premium, MCL 500.2123 requires at least 30 days' notice, and ties the permitted reasons to the closed list in MCL 500.2117.
Under MCL 500.2124, when does civil liability attach to a statement made about the reasons for an insured's cancellation, nonrenewal, or declination?

Only if the statement is shown to have been made with gross negligence, or in bad faith with malice in fact, and was made in one of the three settings listed in MCL 500.2124(2): in the written notice or other communication giving the reasons, in a communication providing information about the action, or in testimony or evidence in a court or administrative proceeding where the action is at issue. Otherwise there is no civil liability.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(q), how long does an insured have to commence an action under a fire policy, and what tolls that period?

1 year after the loss or the time period specified in the policy, whichever is longer. The period is tolled from the time the insured notifies the insurer of the loss until the insurer formally denies liability.
A loss occurs January 5, 2026, and notice is given January 6. The insurer never formally denies the claim. When does the 1-year suit clock actually expire?

It does not run to a fixed date. Only the 1 day between the loss and the notice counts against the year; the clock is tolled from January 6, 2026 onward and stays paused until the insurer formally denies liability.
TRAP: Does a partial payment made with a reservation of rights count as a 'formal denial' that ends tolling under MCL 500.2833(1)(q)?

Not by itself. A reservation-of-rights partial payment is not, by itself, a formal denial. A letter stating the carrier considers the claim closed reads much closer to one. The statute does not define 'formally denies,' so every ambiguous letter should be calendared.
What does DIFS's own complaint page (michigan.gov/difs/consumers/complaint) say its Office of Consumer Services does?

It provides consumer information and investigates consumer complaints, aims to respond promptly and completely, and assists consumers in resolving complaints whenever possible, after first encouraging consumers to try to resolve disputes directly with the carrier.
What is DIFS's phone number and hours for filing an insurance complaint?
877-999-6442, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
TRAP: Does Michigan law or DIFS's own complaint page state that DIFS will make a carrier answer a consumer complaint within 30 days?
No. The DIFS complaint page states no day count for how fast DIFS or the carrier must respond. Any claim that DIFS forces a 30-day answer is INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
What is DIFS actually able to do about a consumer complaint against an insurer, and what does the record NOT show it can do?

Verified: DIFS investigates complaints and assists consumers in resolving them (its complaint page), and it can sanction an insurer with fines and with suspension or revocation of the insurer's certificate of authority (Bulletin 2025-25-INS). Underneath that, MCL 500.2026(1) reaches conduct 'other than isolated incidents' showing 'a persistent tendency,' so one bad claim is not itself the unfair practice, and Young v Michigan Mutual Ins Co, 139 Mich App 600 (1984), says section 2026 exists to give the regulator authority over continuing practices. Nothing DIFS publishes says it can adjudicate coverage, order a specific payment, or act as your lawyer. Treat any such claim as INSUFFICIENT_DATA. A DIFS complaint is leverage and a record, not a ruling.
Under MCL 500.2026(2), what must an insurer maintain about the complaints of its insureds, and what counts as a 'complaint'?

A complete record since the last examination, showing the total number of complaints, their classification by line of insurance, the nature of each complaint, its disposition, and the time it took to process. A 'complaint' means a written communication primarily expressing an allegation of acts that would violate chapter 20.
Under MCL 500.2026(2), what happens if an insurance agent (not also an employee) receives a written complaint about the insurer?
The agent must promptly forward the complaint to the insurer, unless the agent resolves it to the insured's satisfaction within a reasonable time.
Is there a private right of action against an insurer directly under MCL 500.2026?

No private action in tort under section 2026. Young v Michigan Mutual Ins Co, 139 Mich App 600 (1984): 'The insured does not have an independent cause of action under MCL 500.2026'; enforcement runs through the regulator. Young draws the line worth remembering, though: it approves 'a private cause of action to recover the interest penalty in section 2006 of the UTPA.' The 12% is suable. The 14 practices are not.
Under Fannie Mae Servicing Guide B-5-01, what is the initial loss-draft disbursement formula for a loan that is current or less than 31 days delinquent?

The servicer may release an initial disbursement up to the greater of $40,000; 33% of the insurance loss proceeds; or the amount by which the release funds exceed the sum of the unpaid principal balance, accrued interest, and advances on the mortgage loan.
Under Fannie Mae Servicing Guide B-5-01, what is the initial disbursement limit if the loan is 31 or more days delinquent?

If the proceeds are $5,000 or less, the servicer may pay them in one payment. If the proceeds exceed $5,000, the initial release is 25% of the total proceeds, but no more than the greater of $10,000 or the amount by which the release funds exceed the loan's UPB, accrued interest, and advances. The rest goes out in increments of no more than 25% after inspections, and a final inspection is required.
Under Fannie Mae Servicing Guide B-5-01, may a servicer pay a public adjuster's fee out of insurance loss proceeds?

Only if Fannie Mae agrees in writing. The Guide directs servicers to prohibit payment of fees out of insurance loss proceeds to public adjusters or other third parties retained by the borrower, unless otherwise agreed to by Fannie Mae in writing.
TRAP: Is Fannie Mae's Servicing Guide B-5-01 a Michigan statute or DIFS rule?
No. It is a private investor servicing guide that binds mortgage servicers on Fannie-Mae-owned loans. It is not Michigan law and does not bind insurers directly.
What is a DIFS bulletin, legally, and how can it change?
It is the Director's interpretive guidance on how DIFS reads the Insurance Code. It is not a statute, and it can be superseded by a later bulletin with no legislative vote.

Under DIFS Bulletin 2024-26-INS, what must an insurer do before depreciating 'nontangible items' (labor, taxes, fees, overhead and profit) on personal-lines homeowners or dwelling policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2025?

Depreciate them only through a standalone, optional endorsement specifically identifying the nontangible items subject to depreciation, offered for a commensurate reduction in premium, rather than through definitions buried in the policy form.
TRAP: Does DIFS Bulletin 2024-26-INS ban depreciation of labor and overhead and profit on Michigan homeowners policies?
No. It conditions the practice; it does not ban it. Depreciation of nontangible items is still allowed via a standalone, optional, premium-reduced endorsement.
What statutory provisions does DIFS Bulletin 2025-25-INS cite as anchor provisions for improper claims-administration practices?

MCL 500.2026(1)(c) and (f): failing to adopt and implement reasonable standards for prompt investigation, and failing to attempt in good faith a prompt, fair, and equitable settlement where liability has become reasonably clear.
TRAP: Is DIFS Bulletin 2025-25-INS written specifically to govern Michigan property claims?

No. It is titled 'Improper Claims Administration Practices in Automobile Insurance,' and every listed example is auto-specific, most of them about collision and comprehensive total losses and titles. What travels beyond auto is the statute it cites, MCL 500.2026(1)(c) and (f), which is not line-limited. The bulletin itself is not a property bulletin, so do not quote it to a property adjuster as if it were.
Under DIFS Bulletin 2026-16-INS, what is the fire insurance maximum escrow withholding amount effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and under what section?
TRAP: Is the $25,090 figure in Bulletin 2026-16-INS the same escrow as MCL 500.2845's calendar-year escrow?

No. Two different sections, two different figures, two different periods. MCL 500.2227's cap is $25,090 for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 (Bulletin 2026-16-INS). MCL 500.2845's separate calendar-year cap is $16,383 for January 1 through December 31, 2026 (Bulletin 2025-27-INS). Both are 25% municipal fire-escrow programs, both CPI-adjusted, but never interchange the numbers or the sections.
On a water loss reported January 6 with a proof of loss submitted February 1, on what date is the loss payable under the 30-day payment clock?
March 3 (30 days after February 1, the date the proof of amount of loss was received).
On the same water loss (proof of loss received February 1), on what date does 12% interest begin accruing if the claim remains unpaid?
April 2 (60 days after February 1, the date satisfactory proof of loss was received).
On the same water loss, by what date must the insurer have specified in writing any deficiency in the homeowner's proof of loss?
February 5 (30 days after January 6, the date the claim/notice of loss was received).

A homeowner's policy has been in force 4 years. The insurer sends a nonrenewal notice citing 3 paid claims totaling $5,200 over the past 3 years, all hail and windstorm claims. Does that meet MCL 500.2117's nonrenewal claim-history threshold?

No. Strip out the weather-related claims and the exclusive-of-weather total is $0, far below the $5,000 threshold. Counting them all in, the total is $5,200, below the $6,600 including-weather threshold. Neither branch of MCL 500.2117(2)(e)(i) is met, using the CPI-adjusted figures DIFS certified in Bulletin 2024-02-INS effective January 1, 2024. A student who used the statute's printed $3,000 and $4,000 would wrongly say the nonrenewal is supported.
Under MCL 500.2103(2)(g), how long must a home insurance policy have been canceled for nonpayment before a person can be excluded as an 'eligible person' on that basis?
If canceled for nonpayment of premium within the immediately preceding 2-year period, unless the premium due is paid in full before issuance or renewal.
